spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands from northwest to southeast with dark ocean background. Scattered white cumulus and thin cirrus clouds are present, heaviest over the large southeastern island obscuring the summit area, with smaller clouds over the northwestern islands. No distinct gray haze, smoke or volcanic plume is discernible apart from ordinary white clouds.

classify.caveats: No plume found; nothing to classify.

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea has been intermittently erupting bursts of spatter building a small cone around the north vent in Halemaʻumaʻu; no precursory flows since September 12. Summit inflation stalled last night further delaying the onset of episode 55 fountaining. Overview: Intermittent eruptions of spatter bursts built a small cone around the north vent in Halemaʻumaʻu over the past day.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts increased in August, while the summit region showed no other signs of deformation. Mauna Loa had an increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 87 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the August reporting period, after 57 in July. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
